# Wren

> Self-hosted versioned JSON storage, static site deployment, and queryable collections. Every write creates a new immutable version. Deploy files and data together, preview before going live, promote when ready. Query with projection, aggregation, and materialized views. Postgres-backed, deployed with Docker.

This file is the LLM-friendly index for Wren. It is intended for AI agents and tools that want a fast orientation; follow the links below for full detail.

Wren is an open-source backend service that combines versioned JSON storage with static site deployment. Deploy a directory of HTML/CSS/JS files with `wren deploy`, version every change, preview via labels, and promote to published when ready. Collections store structured JSON data alongside your files — one system, one tree, one label controls what's live. Each organization gets its own isolated Postgres schema.

## URL map — read this first

There are exactly three URL families. Do not mix them.

| Family | URL shape | Auth | Org comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| Private API (read + write) | `/api/v1/{collection}…`, `/api/v1/tree/{tree}/{path}`, `/api/v1/me`, `/api/v1/permissions`, `/api/v1/retention`… | `Authorization: Bearer wren_…` or session cookie | the API key / session — never the URL |
| Public data (read-only) | `/api/v1/orgs/{slug}/{collection}…`, `/api/v1/orgs/{slug}/tree/{tree}/{path}` | none | `{slug}` in the URL |
| Public site (read-only) | `/orgs/{slug}/tree/{tree}/{path}` | none | `{slug}` in the URL |

Rules:
- **Every authenticated route starts with `/api/v1/`.** There are no unversioned routes: `/collections`, `/{collection}`, `/api/me`, `/api/keys`, `/api/permissions` all return 404.
- **Public URLs only return what a `principal: "*"` read rule allows**, otherwise 403. Nothing is public by default. Sending an API key to a public URL does not unlock anything more.
- **Public URLs are read-only.** Only GET (and `POST …/_query`) is accepted; writes return 405. Write through the private API.
- `/orgs/{slug}/…` is a GET-only alias of `/api/v1/orgs/{slug}/…`. Give humans `/orgs/{slug}/tree/{tree}/index.html`; in code, use `/api/v1/orgs/{slug}/…` for data (needed for `POST _query`).
- Find your org slug with `GET /api/v1/me` → `org.slug` (needs a key). Every public org also has `GET /orgs/{slug}/llms.txt` describing what it exposes.
- A tree URL returns the raw file (HTML, JSON, image bytes). Send `Accept: application/json` to get the tree node (documentId, collection, children) instead.
- Use `https://`. Public responses are cached briefly at the CDN (`max-age=60`); add `?v=<hash>` to bust caches after a deploy.

## AI agents (MCP)

Every WREN server has a built-in MCP endpoint: `POST https://<host>/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless JSON). One endpoint per server; the org comes from the API key (`Authorization: Bearer wren_…`), and every tool goes through the same permission checks as the REST API. Tools: whoami, list_collections, query_documents, get_document, list_versions, diff_versions, list_tree, read_file, write_document, write_file, set_label, promote_tree. Writes label new versions "preview" by default; promote_tree releases a tree in one transaction (destructive, confirm with the user). `/mcp?readonly=1` exposes only read tools. Without a key, `/mcp` is public and read-only for every org's public data: `list_public` (who publishes what) plus `public_site_info`, `public_list_tree`, `public_read_file`, `public_query_documents`, `public_get_document` (each takes `org`); keyed sessions get these `public_*` tools too, and they never send the key. Browser sign-in instead of a key: `/mcp/login` (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE with dynamic client registration; discovery at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/login`); the user picks the org on WREN's consent page and the client acts as that user there; the token is MCP-only. Users see and revoke their connected apps at `GET/DELETE /api/v1/connected-apps[/{clientId}]` (browser session only; Admin UI → Connected apps). Org-bound variant for custom domains: `/orgs/{slug}/mcp` — without a key public and read-only (`?tree=<name>` scopes it to one site, `&collections=a,b` adds collections); with a key full tools, only for keys of that org. Setup for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code: [/guides/mcp](/guides/mcp).

```
claude mcp add --transport http wren https://<host>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $WREN_API_KEY"
```

## Make something public (recipe)

```
# 1. Who am I / what is my slug?
GET  /api/v1/me                                    → { org: { slug: "brave-fox-hill", … } }

# 2. Allow anonymous reads. Add labelFilter so visitors only see the published version.
POST /api/v1/permissions  {"principal":"*","resource":"tree:mysite","access":"read","labelFilter":"published"}
POST /api/v1/permissions  {"principal":"*","resource":"collection:mydata","access":"read","labelFilter":"published"}

# 3. Public URLs
https://<host>/orgs/brave-fox-hill/tree/mysite/index.html          (site, for people)
https://<host>/api/v1/orgs/brave-fox-hill/mydata?limit=50          (data, for code)
```

- Without `labelFilter`, visitors see the latest version of every document, including unfinished work. With `labelFilter: "published"`, only versions you label `published` are visible, and `?label=` on the URL cannot override it.
- Public access is granted per whole tree or collection. To keep something private, put it in a different tree/collection without a `*` rule.
- `GET /api/v1/projects` (no auth) lists every org with public rules — anything you make public is discoverable there.

## Key concepts

- **Collections** — named document namespaces; schema-free by default, optionally validated with JSON Schema
- **Documents** — JSON objects stored with a UUID; every mutation creates a new version
- **Versions** — immutable snapshots; list, diff, or roll back to any point in history
- **Retention policies** — optional per-org default (`*`) and per-collection rules (keep only labeled, keep newest N, remove older than N days, remove older than a label) that remove old versions hourly; the current version and every labeled version are always kept; preview first with `POST /api/v1/retention/{collection|*}/_preview` (org owner/admin)
- **Labels** — named pointers to a specific version (`published`, `draft`, `staging`, etc.)
- **Trees** — hierarchical path assignment (`/site/about`, `/blog/2026/hello`) for CMS navigation and static site serving
- **Deploy** — `wren deploy ./dist --tree mysite` uploads files, assigns tree paths, and serves the site. `wren promote` moves the published label on every document in the tree in one transaction (`POST /api/v1/tree/{name}/_promote`).
- **Binary assets** — collections can store files (HTML, CSS, JS, images, PDFs) alongside JSON metadata. To publish a new version of a file, `PUT` multipart to the existing document id; `POST` creates a new document. Identical bytes are stored once; re-uploading the same bytes, filename and type creates no version and returns `"unchanged": true`.
- **Multi-tenancy** — each org is isolated in its own Postgres schema; invite collaborators with role-based access
- **$ref resolution** — documents can reference other documents, tree paths, or queries; add `?depth=N` to resolve server-side with loop detection
- **Live events** — Server-Sent Events of every change: `GET /api/v1/_events` (what you can read) and `GET /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/_events` (public: only published label moves). Ids and versions, no data; resume with `Last-Event-ID`
- **Webhooks** — batched HTTP notifications on data changes with HMAC signing, retry, and replay; same events as the streams; public receiver addresses only
- **Permissions** — rules per principal (`*`, `member:<userId>`, `group:<groupId>`, `key:<keyId>`), with optional label/data filters and public aliases
- **Groups** — people get data access through groups (every org starts with Editors = write `*`, Viewers = read `*`); invites choose role (member|admin, what they may manage) and groups (what data). API keys act as their creator; `key:` rules narrow a key. Org admins can impersonate ("view as") a member within the org; changes are recorded with `impersonatedBy`.
- **API keys** — long-lived Bearer tokens, scoped to the org they were created in

## Client libraries

- **CLI**: `npm install -g @usewren/cli` — `wren deploy`, `wren promote`, document and tree commands
- **wren.js** (browser): `<script src="/wren.js">` — zero-dependency web components for declarative data binding (`<wren-list>`, `<wren-query>`, `<wren-materialized>`, `<wren-doc>`, `<wren-tree>`). Auto-detects org from URL; works on custom domains via `data-base` attribute.
- **TypeScript / JavaScript**: `npm install @usewren/client` — Node ≥18, Bun, Browser; zero runtime dependencies; full types
- **Python**: `pip install usewren-client` — Python ≥3.9; sync (`WrenClient`) and async (`AsyncWrenClient`) via httpx; dataclasses

## Authentication

Two methods, both only on `/api/v1/…` private routes:
1. **Bearer token** (API key): `Authorization: Bearer wren_…` — create keys in Admin UI → API Keys, or `POST /api/v1/keys`. A key always acts in the org it was created in.
2. **Session cookie**: `better-auth.session_token=…` — set after `POST /api/auth/sign-in/email`. Switch org with `PUT /api/v1/org`.

Calling from a browser on another domain: public routes allow any origin; private routes accept a Bearer key from any origin (cookies only from the Wren site itself). Never ship an API key in public page code — proxy writes through your own backend.

Calling from scripts: some deployments sit behind Cloudflare, which may reject Python's default `urllib` User-Agent with `403 error code: 1010`. Set a User-Agent (`requests`/`httpx` and curl are fine):

```python
import json, urllib.request
req = urllib.request.Request("https://<host>/api/v1/orgs/<slug>/mydata",
                             headers={"User-Agent": "my-app/1.0", "Accept": "application/json"})
print(json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req)))
```

## Private API reference (all need auth, all under /api/v1)

```
# Identity & org
GET    /api/v1/me                                   principal, org {id, name, slug}, role, applicable rules
GET    /api/v1/org                                  current org + orgs you can switch to
PUT    /api/v1/org                                  {orgId} → switch org (session only)
PUT    /api/v1/org/slug                             {slug} → set public slug
GET    /api/v1/org/usage                            storage / request stats

# Documents
GET    /api/v1/collections                          list collections
GET    /api/v1/{collection}                         list (?label=, ?limit=, ?offset=, ?select=a,b, ?where=field:value)
POST   /api/v1/{collection}                         JSON → new document {id, version:1, …}; multipart (file=) → new binary document
GET    /api/v1/{collection}/{id}                    get document (?label=, ?depth=)
GET    /api/v1/{collection}/{id}/raw                binary bytes (?version=, ?label=)
PUT    /api/v1/{collection}/{id}                    JSON or multipart → new version of the same document
DELETE /api/v1/{collection}/{id}                    soft delete
GET    /api/v1/{collection}/by-key/{value}          get by natural key (collection must declare naturalKey)
PUT    /api/v1/{collection}/by-key/{value}          idempotent upsert by natural key
DELETE /api/v1/{collection}/by-key/{value}          soft delete by natural key

# Versions & labels
GET    /api/v1/{collection}/{id}/versions           list versions
GET    /api/v1/{collection}/{id}/versions/{n}       get version n
POST   /api/v1/{collection}/{id}/rollback/{n}       roll back (creates new version)
GET    /api/v1/{collection}/{id}/diff?v1=N&v2=N     diff two versions
POST   /api/v1/{collection}/{id}/labels             {label, version?} → pin label
DELETE /api/v1/{collection}/{id}/labels/{label}     remove a label
POST   /api/v1/{collection}/{id}/undelete           bring back a deleted document
PATCH  /api/v1/{collection}/_schema                change only the fields sent
       If-Match: "<version>" / ?ifVersion=<n> on PUT/DELETE → 412 if someone wrote in between (ifVersion=0: create-only)
POST   /api/v1/{collection}/_restore                {label, deleteUnlabeled?} → whole collection to a label (one transaction)
POST   /api/v1/tree/{name}/_restore                 {label} → every document in the tree to a label

# Schemas
GET    /api/v1/{collection}/_schema
PUT    /api/v1/{collection}/_schema                 {schema, displayName, collectionType, naturalKey?, indexes?}
DELETE /api/v1/{collection}/_schema
POST   /api/v1/{collection}/_schema/validate        dry-run a schema against existing docs

# Query
POST   /api/v1/{collection}/_query                  filter + projection + aggregation (JSON body; paginate with cursor)

# Materialized queries
GET    /api/v1/{collection}/_materialized           list
PUT    /api/v1/{collection}/_materialized/{name}    create/update (auto-refreshes on write)
GET    /api/v1/{collection}/_materialized/{name}    read result
DELETE /api/v1/{collection}/_materialized/{name}    remove

# Trees
GET    /api/v1/tree                                 list trees
GET    /api/v1/tree/{name}?full=true                full tree snapshot
GET    /api/v1/tree/{name}/{path}                   file bytes; with Accept: application/json → node {documentId, collection, children}
PUT    /api/v1/tree/{name}/{path}                   {documentId} → assign
DELETE /api/v1/tree/{name}/{path}                   unassign
POST   /api/v1/tree/{name}/_promote                 {label?="published", from?} → move label on every doc in one transaction

# Keys, members, invites, permissions, webhooks (act on the key's / session's org)
GET    /api/v1/keys                                 list API keys
POST   /api/v1/keys                                 {name} → create key (shown once)
DELETE /api/v1/keys/{id}                            revoke
GET    /api/v1/members                              list members
DELETE /api/v1/members/{id}                         remove member
GET    /api/v1/invites                              list sent invites
POST   /api/v1/invites                              {email, role?} → invite
DELETE /api/v1/invites/{id}                         revoke invite
POST   /api/v1/invites/accept                       {token} → accept
GET    /api/v1/permissions                          list rules
POST   /api/v1/permissions                          {principal, resource, access, labelFilter?, filterLang?, filterExpr?, alias?}
PUT    /api/v1/permissions/{id}                     update rule
DELETE /api/v1/permissions/{id}                     delete rule
GET    /api/v1/_events?collections=a,b&trees=t     live changes (Server-Sent Events)
GET    /api/v1/webhooks                             list webhooks
POST   /api/v1/webhooks                             create (returns signing secret once)
PUT    /api/v1/webhooks/{id}                        update url/events/enabled
DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/{id}                        delete
GET    /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries             delivery log
POST   /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/replay                 re-deliver past events

# Retention (org owner/admin; {collection} or * for the org default; current + labeled versions always kept)
GET    /api/v1/retention                            {default, collections, runs}
PUT    /api/v1/retention/{collection}               {labeledOnly?, maxVersions?, maxAgeDays?, afterLabel?} → replace policy ({} = keep everything)
DELETE /api/v1/retention/{collection}               remove policy (falls back to the default)
POST   /api/v1/retention/{collection}/_preview      optional proposed rules → {collections, total:{versions, documents, bytes}}; changes nothing
POST   /api/v1/retention/_apply                     remove now (also runs hourly) → same shape as _preview
```

## Public API reference (no auth, read-only, gated by principal "*" rules)

```
GET    /api/v1/projects                             all orgs with public rules, their collections, trees and entry URLs
GET    /orgs/{slug}/llms.txt                        what this org exposes publicly
GET    /orgs/{slug}/tree/{tree}/{path}              site file (alias of /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/tree/…)
GET    /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/tree/{tree}/{path}       file bytes; Accept: application/json → node
GET    /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/tree/{tree}?full=true    full tree snapshot
GET    /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/{collection}             list (?limit=, ?offset=, ?select=, ?where=)
GET    /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/{collection}/{id}        get document
GET    /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/{collection}/{id}/raw    binary bytes
GET    /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/{collection}/by-key/{v}  get by natural key
POST   /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/{collection}/_query      query (same body as private _query)
GET    /api/v1/orgs/{slug}/{collection}/_materialized[/{name}]
```

If a rule has `labelFilter`, every public read above returns the labeled version; `?label=` and `?version=` cannot override it.
